utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Dan Saxon, Salvatore Cannata, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning. Daniela Tasic, Chad Mair, Milos Androvic, and Gregor Guy-Smith on behalf of Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just before we begin may I just mention that we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis today, Judge David being absent and held up in the Lukic and Lukic case. Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I wish to mention for the record that I'm going to call the first of three videolink witnesses scheduled for today, and the Prosecution calls witness Nefa Sljivo. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. They come in that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You may call them. Is there anything we need to do to make sure?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, the that's the witness I called, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning Madam Registrar out in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please ask the witness to make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not hear the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I've just been -- I was rising for the same reason, but I have just been assisted in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Then I need to be assisted as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, interpreters. I must say, I also heard just a whisper from the witness. If we could be assisted, all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could just -- could you say something that -- out there, Madam Witness. Let's hear whether we can hear you. Madam Sljivo. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters still do not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness can't be heard by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dobro jutro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do I get the attention of the registrar out there?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] I can hear you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's try again. Madam Registrar, could you please get the witness to make the declaration. Hopefully we can hear her this time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may now be seated. I assume that the interpreters did hear her this time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You may proceed, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Madam Witness, good morning. Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, can you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Nefa Sljivo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ma'am. Now, do you remember giving two statements to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY; the first on the 8th of March, 1997, and the second on the 26th of April, 2006. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can 65 ter 9401 be shown to the witness and placed on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, Madam Witness, do you see a document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see your signature there?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we now move to page 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, is this a statement that you, Witness, gave to the Bosnian authorities about the incident of the 1st of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we have the English translation of this statement up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: It can be found at page 6 of the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you mean of the same document, Mr. Cannata?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Of 65 ter 9401.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, the English version is something separate. Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, do you see your signature on that document, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, did you have an opportunity to review both the Bosnian statement and the ICTY statement before appearing today?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And do you confirm that these statements are true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And would you say the same if you were asked the same -- to speak about the same events today?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, can 65 ter number 9410 be given an exhibit number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 9401 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2305.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, just so we're clear, as I understand that particular exhibit, you are confining yourself only to the statement made by Ms. Nefa; correct? Which is pages -- pages one and two of the English and then the -- one page of the BiH [sic]. It's a three-page. You will be introducing three pages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm introducing the whole statement, 65 ter number 9401 which consists of the ICTY statement, dated 8 of March, 1997, appended to the ICTY statement there's the Bosnian authority statement. And that's the document that I showed to the witness, and I would ask for the admission of the entire document, 9401 which consists of these two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, maybe I'm having some difficulty here, and if I could have but a moment. To the extent that the Prosecution is seeking to introduce the statements of the witness herself, there is no objection. To the extent there is any other documentation, there is an objection because this is not the witness's statement and not something that the witness would testify to. My difficulty is the document I'm looking at contains information, if I'm not mistaken, which is above and beyond the witness's statement. Perhaps I'm looking at the wrong information. So let me just double-check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just be --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's no difficulty. It's taken care of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, you said this is 2305. I thought 65 ter 5830 already has that exhibit number. Shouldn't it be 306?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's correct, 65 ter number 9401 would then become exhibit P2306.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can 65 ter number 9402 be shown to the witness and placed on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Again, Madam Witness, do you have a document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you see your signature there?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review this statement before appearing today?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you confirm that this statement is true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And if you were asked to speak about the same events today, would you give the same answer?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may 65 ter number 9402 be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2307.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter number 9403. And while we're waiting for the document to be produced --

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Madam Witness, let me ask you, do you recall testifying in the case before this Tribunal called Prosecutor versus Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, do you have a copy of the transcript in front of you right now?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this testimony before appearing today?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, can we move to page 4 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, Madam Witness, when we met last week, I understand that it was a small correction that you wish to make to line 20. Now, at line 20 you state that the hospital where you were brought after the incident was called Enver Maric. But when we met, you told me that you probably made a mistake, as can you only remember that the hospital was called Maric. But you cannot remember whether its full name was in fact Enver Maric or not. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, with this small correction, would you be able to confirm that the transcript is true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Would you give the same answers today if you were asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have 65 ter number 9403 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, Madam, last questions from my side. During the testimony, your previous testimony, in the Dragomir Milosevic case, do you recall being shown a medical document?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: You mean from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes. And to assist you, let me have 65 ter 8596 be shown to you and placed on the e-court, please. Now, is that the document that was shown to you during the Dragomir Milosevic case, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Is this document true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May 65 ter number 8596 be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2309, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now with your leave, Your Honour, I will read a short summary of Witness Sljivo's evidence, and that will conclude my examination-in-chief of this witness. Thank you. Witness, Nefa Sljivo has given evidence in respect of scheduled incident A8 of the indictment, that is the incident occurred on the 1st of July, 1995, in Sarajevo, when the explosion of a modified air bomb at Bunicki Potok Street in the Hrasnica area of Sarajevo resulted in the wounding of 13 civilians, including witness Sljivo herself and other members of her family. Witness testified that there were no Bosnian army soldiers or positions in the vicinity of the area hit by the modified air bomb launched on 1st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I have no further questions for you at this time. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning. You were living in, I believe, the area known as Hrasnica; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in the area that you were living, there were soldiers from the ABiH army; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes. But not there where the bomb was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question was: And in the area that you were living there were soldiers from the ABiH army; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: In Hrasnica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this neighbourhood that you were living in, it's at the bottom of Mount Igman. True?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And there's a road that goes by the street of your home, which is a road that is taken in order go up Mount Igman; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: There are several roads in Hrasnica by which you can reach Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during the time that you were living at your home in Hrasnica, did you have occasion to see members of the ABiH on this road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which road? I don't think you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The roads that go up Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. But she said there were several.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The roads. Now I'm referring to the roads that go up Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see members of the army go up that road, of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean going by the road. Are you -- do you mean in columns or ... I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... columns that would be a good question, yes.

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Not where I was nearby anywhere, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have the occasion to see members of the ABiH using this road driving white vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you see members of the ABiH army using these roads driving white vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just -- Mr. Guy-Smith, if you could just hold on. My screen is frozen. I'm not getting the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: If I may assist, the LiveNote is working. I think the e-court transcripts are frozen. But transcripts available on LiveNote which you can access from your black bottom next to the computer, that works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're talking English, I don't understand. I mean ... I can see that LiveNote is working this side, but I use this screen for exhibits, because it's operated from down there. And I'm not able to operate it on the right -- precisely because I don't understand your English, and I -- my LiveNote goes on my right side. That one is frozen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm told it's a universal problem within the Tribunal. Let's go on and see how we go. The one side of the LiveNote is working.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I need to find a screen which is, at the present time, not locked. Which I don't have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The one next to the one that is locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ... if I do that, Your Honour, then I can't see the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, I know. Yeah. You got to sacrifice one of the two things. And you want to observe demeanour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be nice, would be of some assistance to me, in terms of my examination. Let me see if we can do something else. Just let me try something. I don't know if it's going to work or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Guy-Smith, you have four screens in front of you. If can you use the one for LiveNote, and the -- the other one from the other pair --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what we're trying to do right now. This one screen, which is the dedicated screen for the video, is now the screen in which we have LiveNote. I think we're almost there, Your Honour. We're just reconfiguring our computers here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That will work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that we left off before the technical problem, and I apologise for that occurring, with me asking you a question as to whether or not you saw white vehicles being driven by the ABiH army going by the roads up Mount Igman. And -- by your house on the roads going up Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: No. The white car was an UN vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were living in Hrasnica, did you have occasion to use a tunnel to go to town?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many times did you use that tunnel?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I was a student there, so I went into town to go to the uni. I don't know how many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you used the tunnel, were you allowed to go through the tunnel freely, or did you have to obtain a pass to go through that tunnel?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I had to obtain a pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the pass that you obtained, where did you get that pass?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: In the municipality, from the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I understand your testimony, when you used the tunnel, you were going from outside the town, inside the town to go to university; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: But not every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. Did you have to, when you were using the tunnel, did you have to wait to get through the tunnel, or were you able to go through the tunnel freely. And by wait, I mean did you have to wait for a period of time because there were people or cars going through that tunnel?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Vehicles couldn't go through the tunnel. Only people could. And, yes, I did have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And were you -- when you went through the tunnel, did you go through the tunnel in groups of people? And by that I mean was there a wait for 50 or 100 people before they went through the tunnel together?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I don't know how they organised it. In any case there was a group of people, you know. You could not walk in two directions at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I understand your testimony correctly, would it be fair to say that when you went to the university, you went from your home, which was outside of the city, through the confrontation lines, inside the city, through the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Too late. The witness answered. But my point is that the witness never mentioned the confrontation lines in her testimony so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you not mentioned confrontation line. Do you remember when testifying -- when you were testifying you were asked the following question by Judge Harhoff concerning your mode of travel: "I would like to put one short question to you relating to the passage through the tunnel. And if I understand you correctly, because your residence was outside the city, and your university where you studied was within the city, the confrontation lines of the city, you sometimes pass through the tunnel when you wanted to move from the inner city to your home, your residence. Is that correct?" Your answer was: "Could you please repeat your question. Excuse me?" Judge Harhoff then asked you the following question: "That's all right. I understand you to say that you were studying at the university which I suppose was located within the confrontation line, that is to say, in the city centre somewhere, yet your family was living outside. So in order to get from the university to your family residence, you would have to go through the tunnel, and you did so, as I understand, once?" Answer: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: "Every month or so, and you said that." Is that a correct -- is that a correct recitation of the questions that were asked and the answers that you gave in your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. I know that I didn't go every day and that I didn't go often. I had to spend some time at the uni, and then when that was done I would go back. I don't remember how often that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. To your knowledge, were there other tunnels that existed in the city of Sarajevo, where either civilians or the army could pass through the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. During the time that you were in the tunnel, did you have an opportunity to see army members transporting military supplies through this tunnel?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the pass that you received from the civilian authorities, is that a pass that was good for one trip through the tunnel, or is that a pass that was good for a week, or a month? How did that pass work?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I took a pass in Hrasnica every time I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were there times that you went to Hrasnica to get a pass when you weren't allowed a pass because there were -- all the passes had been taken up?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I was a student, which entitled me to a pass every time. And I did get it every time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you sit here today, could you tell us what other kinds of individuals were entitled to have a pass to go through the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata, any further re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question to ask you, Ms. Sljivo. Can you tell me what was the distance between your home in Hrasnica and the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: NEFA SLJIVO
utterances.text: About 4 kilometres. Thereabouts, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That was all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata, any questions arising from the Judge's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, thank you very much. And I thank the judge for her question. I think it's most helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Witness, thank you so much for taking the time to come and testify. We are now done with your testimony. You are now excused and stand down. Please go well back home, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's still lots of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May we go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Looks like Madam Registrar is doubling up as court usher as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you please ask the witness to make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Alija Holjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, can 65 ter number 9409 be shown to the witness and placed on the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY on the 22nd of February, 1996?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And do you see your signature on the document that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review that document before appearing today?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity on the 21st. Two of your officers came, and we sat in my house, and we looked at all of those transcripts. And we looked at them, and we read them through.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, can you confirm that this statement is true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: All the statements that I gave, I stand by them, and I assert that they are truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let me take one statement -- you know, statement by statement, all right? Now I'm talking about the one that you have in front of you. Is that true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you give the same statement today if you were asked to speak about the same events today?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I think that I gave the statements. I stand by them, as I said, these are statements from about ten years back. Perhaps I might miss something, but I was the one who gave these statements, and I stand by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now can I have 65 ter 9409 be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P2312, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we -- can the witness be shown 65 ter number 9410.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 9410.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, again, do you see your signature in that document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes. It's my signature on this document. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I looked through all of these documents on the 21st of April in my apartment with your staff members.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And would you confirm that this statement is true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Everything that I stated, I assert that is accurate and truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And would you say the same today if asked to speak about the same events again?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I gave a statement three times, and I confirm that. If I were to give the statements again, perhaps something I might omit, I'm an elderly, sick man, so I cannot think and remember exactly what happened a year ago, never mind ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May I ask this document be admitted into evidence. It's 9410, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that the answer just given does not comply with the requirements of Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Let me ask the question again to the witness then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking you about the statement that you have in front of you, all right? Yeah. Now what I'm --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now, would you, if I were to ask you today to speak about the same events on the 27th of February, 1995, would you give me the same statement today?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, I would give the same statement that I gave on the 27th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Now can I have this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted -- yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, therein lies a different problem. The the statement that we're referring to is dated 25th April, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell what is the date of the statement in front of you? Can you look at the B/C/S document that you have in front of you. Can you tell me what is the date on that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And I ask for Madam Registrar's assistance in that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The -- I think that the date is the 25th of April, 1996. That's when the statement was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can this document be admitted now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the correct date?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not according to the information I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was a translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, it wasn't a translation error. And I suggest you don't mention any different dates until the witness can testify about what he is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, can you please read for me what is the date of the document that is in front of you right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It may now be admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P2313.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown now 65 ter 9408 and that document be placed on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a document? Do you have a document? Yes. I see that. Now, can you --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you describe what that document is?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: This is the document -- or, rather, the statement that I provided on the 27th of February, 1995, when things happened around 12.35 when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand that answer. I don't -- what does that date refer to? To the date he gave the statement, or to the date he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date when I was wounded, on the 27th of February, 1995, at 1235 hours. That's when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And by looking at this document, do you see your signature here?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have an opportunity it review this document before coming today to the field office?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes. I've told you that I had a time to look at all the statements. You -- your officers gave them to me when they came up to me, to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you confirm that this statement is true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I can confirm this. That's why I provided this statement, and I can confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And would you stand by the statement again today, if asked to speak about the same events, on the 27th of February, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I would provide answers to the effect as it was during the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Would you -- would you say -- would you give the same statement as the one that you gave to the Bosnian authorities, and that is in front of you, if I asked you today to speak what happened to you on the 27th of February, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I'm not denying anything that I said in that statement. I would give the same statement. I can't say one thing now and the other thing next time. Everything has to be the same, now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Now can I have this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P2314, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can I have the witness be shown 65 ter number 9411.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, again, do you recall testifying in case Prosecutor versus Dragomir Milosevic on 2007?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I provided the statements that are before me now, and that's all. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Let -- just listen to my question, please, and answer them. Now, I ask you whether you recalled testifying, like you are doing today from Nedzarici, in a previous case, which is the case Prosecutor versus Dragomir Milosevic. It was in 2007. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, have you testified before the Tribunal from the Sarajevo field office in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, I did testify in Nedzarici, but I can't remember when it was. That's what I'm saying. I don't know when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember what was the case that you testified about?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't know what case it was. I don't remember, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you want to do with 9411?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I withdraw the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could have two seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually, I forgot to read out the summary for this witness, in light of the previous documents submitted through him, the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I was saying, Mr. Guy-Smith, your colleague has forgotten something which he would like to read before he gives you an opportunity to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand, and I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness Alija Holjan has given evidence in respect of scheduled incident B10 of the indictment, that is the sniping incident occurred on the 27th of February, 1995, in Sarajevo when a tram was attacked by sniper fire when travelling on Zmaja od Bosne, from Stari Grad to Novi Grad, which is westbound direction. This sniping attack resulted in the wounding of Witness Holjan and several other civilians. Witness Holjan testified that the fire came from the direction of the Grbavica sky-scrapers --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. Now we have a difficulty because he hasn't testified. There is no testimony. There are three statements, but there's no testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the summary, I believe if I'm not mistaken, this part of the statement now is incorrect. Because we don't have that information contained in his -- in his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But isn't this information contained in his statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me double-check. I don't believe the thing that was just said is contained in the statement. I don't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: If I might assist. It is now P2313, which is the statement of the 22nd February 1996 -- actually, I'm sorry, it's 2312, the statement of 22 February, 1996, and it's the fourth paragraph, first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Actually concluded my sort summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I thought -- I thought you were still speaking when Mr. Guy-Smith stood up. You said witness Holjan testified that the fire came from the direction of the Grbavica sky-scrapers. Is that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Full stop. Any cross-examination, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There will be none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No cross-examination, okay. Questions for the witness? Mr. Holjan, thank you very much for taking time from your very busy schedule to come and testify, and this brings us now to the end of your testimony. You are excused. You may stand down. Once again, thank you, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I will -- with your leave, I will ask Mr. Dan Saxon to address you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, obviously, these witnesses went much more quickly than the Prosecution anticipated. The next witness is a closed session witness, and I'm told he has not yet arrived in The Hague. Therefore, we -- I would ask that we adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow morning, and -- to call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Court adjourned to tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning. Now, just before we adjourn, there was a bit of confusion this morning. I'm not sure whether we're sitting in Courtroom II tomorrow or Courtroom I. I had it as Courtroom I today and tomorrow, and we are now in Courtroom II. Okay. Then we stand adjourned to Courtroom II tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th of April, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.18 p.m.,
